p1s.summary: The censoring bound the paper puts in front of every clean-design count is measured on the DEFAULT-depth alignment screen (7 failures, 47 of 183 assessable), but the paper's only clean-design count — 'Three designs clear every screen' — is computed on the DEEP screens, which have a different set of three failures and no censoring at all. Worse, one of the three named clean designs is itself one of the seven the paper says 'never returned'.
p1s.evidence: Re-derived by enumerating the 38 default-depth 5-6-5 screens research/modalities/junction-aso-offtarget-<junction>.json: 190 design rows, status counts {screened: 183, screen_failed: 7}, and 47 of the 183 screened rows carry a stored hit list at least as long as their reported near-match count (uncensored). Both figures reproduce the manuscript exactly, so the numbers themselves are right for that tier. The seven failures are AGGGCATATCACCAGG / GCATATCACCAGGCTT / CAGGGCATATCACCAG at EWSR1_e9, CAGGGCATATTGTTCT at FUS_e3, GGGCATATCTCGCCGC at TAF15_e12, GGGCATATCAAGCGCT at TCF12_e7, and GGCATATCTTGCATAA at TCF12_e9. Enumerating the 38 deep (deep500/clean9) 5-6-5 screens gives a different picture: 190 rows, {screened: 187, screen_failed: 3} — the three being CAGGGCATATCTCCAC and GCATATCTCCACCTCC at FUS_e5 and AGGGCATATCTTCATC at TFG_e2 — and all 187 hit lists are complete (0 censored). research/modalities/aso-per-junction-table.json, which joins the five screens at the deep tier, holds 187 design rows and names those same three as 'designs_absent_because_the_deep_screen_did_not_return'. Filtering that table for designs with no hybridisable near-match, no precursor gap-paired hit, no genome named-target site and a mature-parent duplex below ten base pairs returns exactly the paper's three: AGGGCATATCGGAGTC at FUS_e8 (parent duplex 0), GGGCATATCCGACATG at TAF15_e1 (0) and GGGCATATCAAGCGCT at TCF12_e7 (8 bp, wild-type NR4A3) — so the count of three is correct, and it rests on 187 assessable records, not on 47 of 183. GGGCATATCAAGCGCT appears in both lists: it is the sixth of the seven default-screen failures AND one of the three designs the paper reports as clearing every screen. The companion extended report states the reconciliation the journal article omits (research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:509-515: 'Seven of the 190 designs had failed at the remote service and carried no count at all … all seven returned at the deeper ceiling, six of them dirty and one (5'-GGGCATATCAAGCGCT-3' at TCF12 exon 7) with three near-matches and none on the sense strand'), so within the journal article alone 'never returned' is unqualified and contradicted by the paper's own candidate list. The defect is presentational, not arithmetic: the three deep-tier failures are all independently condemned by the mature-parent screen (12 bp against NR4A3, 10 bp against TAF15 and 11 bp against NR4A3 respectively, from research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json), so none of them could have been a fourth clean design and the value three is exact rather than a floor.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The fix is to say which tier each denominator belongs to — 'seven of the 190 default-ceiling alignment screens never returned' and 'the deeper pass returned 187 of 190 with every hit list complete, and decided six of the seven' — not to change any number. The silent-regression risk is the opposite edit: dropping 'default' from the second bound's 'most designs clean at the default search ceiling', or re-tiering the clean count to the default screens (where the same filter returns nine, not three, per the submission plan's 'Nine designs at six junctions carry no hybridisable near-match'), would silently swap the denominator under a sentence that reads unchanged. Nothing in the repository binds the tier of the 7/183/47 triple to the tier of the clean count: they are computed by different modules over different screen files, and the guard that pins the censoring derivation is scoped to the extended report alone (noted at research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-guard-coverage-audit.md:184), so the journal article's copy is unmeasured.
p1s.where: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:196-201 (the two bounds) against :222-224 (the three clean designs)

p1s.summary: The cover letter's live status banner — the one non-superseded block in a document `submission_packet.py` lists as a required submission item — names a superseded, never-published DOI as the one 'both papers now cite' and states that the papers' archive links 'resolve to nothing'. Both halves are false at the pin.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-cover-letter.md:25-41 is the file's only status block not wrapped in a '⚠ *Superseded, retained (rule 1.2)*' marker (the four that follow it, at :43, :50, :61, :68, all are). It reads: 'Both papers now cite **10.5281/zenodo.22180100**, a RESERVED BUT UNPUBLISHED version ... Until it is published the archive links in both papers resolve to nothing.' Re-derived against the pin: (a) WHICH DOI THE PAPERS CITE — `grep -n 'zenodo\.[0-9]*'` over the deliverables returns 10.5281/zenodo.22229096 and nothing else at fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:411, fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:2602 and :2757, fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv:38 and .fasta:37; pdfminer over the three built PDFs returns the single token 'zenodo.22229096' in the journal-article and preprint builds (the anonymized build correctly carries none). 22180100 appears in NO deliverable. (b) WHETHER IT RESOLVES — GitHub Actions run 33560898366, job 100032854734, `zenodo_verify.py` against the public records API, verbatim: 'record 22229096 — 10.5281/zenodo.22229096', 'state : done (submitted=True)', 'published : 2026-09-01', 'type : dataset', 'files : 1 emc-aso-archive.zip 8808345 bytes md5:957ae067bc96c964', 'PUBLISHED. The DOI both papers cite resolves to this record.' That matches deposit-state.json `published.doi`/`published.published` exactly. Direct resolution could not be attempted from this sandbox (doi.org and zenodo.org are both EGRESS_BLOCKED at the proxy), so the Actions log is the reading. Nothing binds the cover letter's identifier: `lint_citations.py` exits 0 with the stale DOI present (it anchors identifiers to a fetch, and 22180100 is anchored by deposit-state.json's superseded-versions list; currency is not one of its axes), and no test under research/manuscripts/tests or scripts/tests names the cover letter together with a DOI or 'zenodo'.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The regression already happened and is silent by construction: this sentence turns over every time a new archive version is minted, and the file itself records that it has turned over three times before ('the third time this sentence has turned over on a new identifier'). Any future repoint of `deposition_doi` moves the papers, the sequence files, the manifest and deposit-state — all of which are checked — and leaves this banner untouched, because it is the only site of that identifier with no producing artifact and no guard. Fixing it by hand fixes only this turn; the fix that holds is to generate the banner from deposit-state.json, or to add a guard that the cover letter names no zenodo DOI other than the current `deposition_doi`.

p1s.summary: The genome-wide screen's exact-match stratum is omitted from the article, and it is the stratum in which one NAMED reagent carries a perfect 16/16, strand-agreeing, gap-fully-paired site inside an annotated lncRNA. The article reports only the raw <=2-mismatch count it then discounts, and its discounting rationale ('most of it never transcribed') does not reach that site.
p1s.evidence: Re-derived from research/modalities/aso-genome-offtarget.json. The article's only genome sentence is 'The genome-wide screen does not separate them: 156 hybridisable gap-paired sites against 135' (line 162); I confirm counts.hybridisable_gap_paired_le2 = 156 (GGGCATATCATCAAAC) and 135 (GGGCATATCTTGTGTG). The same artifact's per_design block gives, for the EWSR1 reagent, counts.exact = 1 and one exact_site: chr3:176354948-176354963, orientation sense, mismatches 0, gap_mismatches 0, gap_fully_paired true, hybridisable true, genes ['ENSG00000304430'], biotypes ['lncRNA'], compartment intronic, softmask_fraction 0.0. The TAF15 reagent has counts.exact = 0. Panel-wide I counted 236 exact sites over 97 of 176 designs, of which 93 are hybridisable AND gap-fully-paired, spread over 58 designs (44 protein-coding intronic, 38 lncRNA intronic, 7 lncRNA exonic, 4 protein-coding exonic). The producing artifact's own headline calls this 'the four strata below are what this screen can actually say' and names stratum 1 'the class the core_nt arm could never reach'. The companion research article DOES report it and adds the warning the journal article lacks — 'a reagent should be read from its own row rather than from the mean' (fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:950-955). Neither the journal article nor its SI contains the words 'exact', '16/16' or 'lncRNA' in this sense (grepped). The asymmetry is the tell: the article discloses a WEAKER site for the same molecule — the two-mismatch TAF15 precursor hit, which I confirmed at aso-premrna-offtarget.json per_design (mismatches 2, gap_mismatches 1, gap_fully_paired false) — while omitting the zero-mismatch one. Note in fairness that 1 exact site is AT chance (artifact's expected_per_design = 1.37305, o/e = 0.7283), so this is an omission of a per-reagent reading, not evidence of an excess.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing in the repository binds the article's genome paragraph to the strata the artifact computes. A future re-run of aso_genome_offtarget.py that moves the exact site (a new assembly patch, a changed annotation release, or a different softmask reference) would silently change which named reagent carries one, and the article would read identically either way. Conversely, if this finding is fixed by adding one sentence naming the site, that sentence is bound to nothing: adding a design, changing MAX_MISMATCHES, or restricting the scan would leave the sentence in place and stale. Any repair should read the count out of aso-genome-offtarget.json['per_design'][*]['counts']['exact'] rather than typing it.

p1s.summary: Every screen the paper rests on is substitution-only — no insertion, deletion or bulged duplex is searched anywhere — and the article states that bound for exactly one of the five screens and never names it in the Limitations. The energy re-scoring additionally DISCARDS gapped alignments, and the article does not say so.
p1s.evidence: Article line 114 states the bound only for screen 2: 'complete for substitutions within a one-mismatch budget'. Grepping the whole article for 'insertion|deletion|bulge|indel|gapped' returns that line and nothing else; the three-limit Limitations paragraph (line 366) names cleavage-vs-hybridisation, nil method novelty and delivery, and does not name search-space shape. Re-derived from the producing code and artifacts: aso-premrna-offtarget.json['method']['blind_to'] lists 'insertions and deletions' explicitly; aso-genome-offtarget.json['method']['algorithm'] is 'the complete <=2-substitution neighbourhood' (substitution-only by construction); aso_parent_gap_pairing.py compares ungapped 16-nt windows, so it cannot represent a bulge; aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json['method']['records_not_scored'] begins 'gapped alignments', and its summary carries n_records_unscorable = 110 of 23331. The companion research article states the generalisation the journal article does not: 'screens 2 to 5 ... are substitution-only by construction' and '110 retained alignments carry an indel and 28 of those are counted as gap-paired sense-strand matches' (fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:2289-2295). So every number the article reports as a liability count — 87, 19, 93, 8, 45, 123 against 8, 156 against 135 — is bounded by a search shape the reader is never told about, and the 8/45 energy classes are computed after 110 records were dropped.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: This is an omission, so nothing regresses it — but a repair is fragile in the same way. A sentence saying 'all five screens are substitution-only' would be silently falsified if the alignment arm's counts were ever taken directly from blastn (which returns gapped alignments and, per the companion article, already retains 110 of them) rather than through the energy module that drops them. Any fix should say which arms are substitution-only BY CONSTRUCTION (2, 3, 4, 5) and that arm 1's gapped hits are dropped at re-scoring, matching aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json['summary']['n_records_unscorable'].

p1s.summary: The gap-length paragraph's headline invariance — 'the liable count holds at 87, 88 and 87' — is an artifact of a threshold that does not scale with the gap, and the producing artifact says in terms that the other reading must be reported alongside it. Under the geometry-invariant criterion the liability falls from 181 designs to 130 to 87, a four-fold drop in rate that would weaken the paper's own negative and is not shown.
p1s.evidence: Re-derived from research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json['geometries']. The three geometries' mature_parent_whole_gap_duplex blocks give n_at_or_above_min_duplex_bp = 87, 88, 87 over 190, 266, 342 designs (45.79%, 33.08%, 25.44% — the article's 45.8/33.1/25.4, confirmed). The SAME blocks give n_with_any_gap_pairing_window = 181, 130, 87, i.e. 95.3%, 48.9%, 25.4% under 'can a wild-type parent pair the whole catalytic gap at all', which is the criterion whose meaning does not change with gap length. The artifact's own _geometry._note says: 'MIN_DUPLEX_BP is an ABSOLUTE hybrid length and does NOT scale with the gap ... at a gap of 10 the catalytic gap alone is already a 10 bp hybrid, so every gap-pairing window clears the threshold by construction ... at a gap of 6 a window needs four further flanking pairs to reach it. Both readings are real and they are not the same reading, so compare geometries on the raw longest_parent_duplex_bp_through_gap distribution as well.' The article carries half of that caveat — it says the 5-10-5 figure 'is a floor' — but not the half that matters for the comparison: at 5-6-5 the criterion is gap + 4 flanking pairs and at 5-10-5 it is gap + 0, so the constancy of 87/88/87 compares three different stringencies. The direction of the omission flatters the paper's claim, since 'Lengthening the catalytic gap does not remove this liability' reads as invariance and the uniform reading shows a four-fold reduction.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: aso_gap_length_tradeoff.py imports MIN_DUPLEX_BP from aso_parent_gap_pairing rather than typing it, so a future change to the 10-bp criterion would move all three counts together and the article's '87, 88 and 87' would go stale with no gate firing on it — the three numbers are typed in prose and bound to nothing. A repair that adds the 181/130/87 series has the same exposure and should be generated, not typed.

p1s.summary: The pre-registered primary endpoint is a ratio whose denominator the paper never establishes is measurable in any test article it names. Selectivity is defined as wild-type NR4A3 over fusion 'in the same wells', but three of the five named test articles are heterologously over-expressed fusion cDNAs whose recipient background is never named and whose wild-type NR4A3 expression is never stated, and the two articles that unambiguously carry a wild-type allele are at the wrong acceptor.
p1s.evidence: Article line 319: 'Selectivity is the ratio of two half-maximal knockdown concentrations: wild-type NR4A3 over the fusion, from a matched dose-response in the same wells.' Grepping the article for 'wild-type NR4A3' returns only the Discussion's screen sentences and 'the patient's own un-rearranged NR4A3 allele' at line 354, which is about a search compartment and not about a test article; grepping for 'endogenous', 'recipient', 'tBJ', 'retroviral' returns only line 264's caveat about the fusion arm. The three engineered articles are verbatim cDNA constructs — research/modalities/emc-test-article-routes.json, route R3, construct_spec_verbatim from PMC6766969: 'The following cDNAs, cloned into the retroviral PLPCX vector ... E-N, corresponding to EWSR1 (exons 1-12)-NR4A3 (exons 3-8) ... T-N*, corresponding to the commonest TAF15 (exons 1-6)-NR4A3 (exons 3-8)'; the same artifact records the background only as 'tBJ/ER ... maintained and engineered by retroviral infections as described', a detail the article does not carry. The article's stated caveat covers the numerator only — 'a heterologously over-expressed complementary DNA speaks to junction-selective knockdown of the intended transcript, not to activity at an endogenous locus' (line 263-264) — and says nothing about whether the ratio's wild-type arm exists in those cells. The two patient-derived models that certainly carry an un-rearranged allele are at NR4A3 exon 2 (research/modalities/emc-model-junction-evidence.json, both models, verbatim from PMC9813045), which the article itself says is not this panel's acceptor. So the experiment the paper offers as its falsification route may have no article in which its own endpoint is defined.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: aso_falsification_power.py binds CUT and SIGMA and derives the four power/void figures (I re-ran it from a scratch copy: n=3 power 30.42%, n=6 81.28%; void_sd 0.648/1.534/2.250 — the article's 30%/80% and 0.65/1.53/2.25, confirmed), but nothing in the repository binds the ENDPOINT DEFINITION to the test-article list. Editing either section alone leaves the other consistent-looking: a future change of test article, or of the acceptor the panel designs against, would not disturb the ratio sentence, and re-pinning the cut would not disturb the test-article section.

p1s.summary: The pre-registration's power and void-SD figures are stated without naming the quantity the 0.35 standard deviation is a standard deviation OF, and without the type-I framing the sibling document carries. Reading it as the per-arm log-IC50 SD rather than the log-ratio SD moves the six-replicate power from 81% to 53%, and the paper gives a referee nothing in this document that decides between the two.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:322-324 reads 'At an assumed replicate standard deviation of 0.35 on the natural-log scale ... six independent biological replicates give about 80% power to falsify a true selectivity of 3 and three give about 30%.' The measurand is never named. The producing module research/manuscripts/aso_falsification_power.py fixes it implicitly and only in code: power_pct() forms ncp = (log 3 - log 5) * sqrt(n) / sigma and void_sd() forms log(5)*sqrt(n)/t_{0.975,n-1}, i.e. sigma is the per-replicate SD of the log SELECTIVITY RATIO, not of either arm's log IC50. Re-run in my scratch copy (statistics_power.py, a byte copy of the module): n=3 power 30.42%, n=6 81.28%, n=10 98.31%; void_sd 0.648 / 1.534 / 2.250 — every printed figure reproduces exactly, so the ARITHMETIC is right and only its stated referent is missing. Sensitivity, computed the same way: at sigma = 0.35*sqrt(2) = 0.495 (the value implied if 0.35 were each arm's log-IC50 SD and the two arms were independent) the same function returns 18.65% / 53.13% / 82.68% — the headline 'about 80%' becomes 'about 50%'. The sibling extended report states exactly what the journal article drops, at research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:1812-1826: 'the replicate standard deviation of its natural logarithm is the quantity to estimate in a pilot, and that standard deviation — taken across independent biological replicates of the same matched dose-response, in the same wells ...', and 'The bound that decides falsification is the upper limit of a two-sided 95% interval, equivalently a one-sided 97.5% bound, so the test's one-sided type-I rate is 2.5% rather than 5%; the figures above are for that bound and change if a one-sided 95% bound is used instead.' Neither clause survives into the journal article: the deciding bound appears there only in the NEXT sentence and only attached to the void figures (:326, 'the upper limit of a two-sided 95% interval below 5'), recovered for the power figures only by the anaphoric 'Those figures are computed on that interval' at :328, and the 2.5% one-sided rate is absent altogether. This matters operationally as well as editorially, because the gate the paper prescribes at :330-331 — 'the gate applies to the upper confidence bound on a pilot's standard deviation: at or above the void figure for the count proposed, the decision is more replicates or no test' — instructs a laboratory to compare a pilot SD against 0.65/1.53/2.25 without saying which statistic to compute for the comparison.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: This is already the regressed state rather than a prospective risk, and the guard surface is why it is invisible. research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py::test_the_falsification_power_and_void_figures_are_the_modules_own binds the five NUMBERS (via _nearest_ten(power_pct(6)), _nearest_ten(power_pct(3)) and f'{void_sd(n):.2f}') and nothing binds the SENTENCE that names their measurand or their type-I rate — a grep of research/manuscripts/tests and research/modalities/tests for 'natural-log', 'two-sided 95' and '97.5' returns no assertion against the journal article's prose. So the clause can be added and later lost again with every gate green. The forward-looking half is the one-of-a-pair shape: the correct wording exists in the sibling at research-article.md:1812-1826, so any repair must move both documents together or the pair diverges again, and a future change of CUT, SIGMA or TRUE_SELECTIVITY in aso_falsification_power.py would silently update the numbers in the article while leaving whatever narrative sentence is added around them stale.
